claim: Endothelial cells line all blood vessels, where they coordinate blood vessel formation and the blood-tissue barrier via regulation of cell-cell junctions.
source: Endothelial cells line all blood vessels, where they coordinate blood vessel formation and the blood-tissue barrier via regulation of cell-cell junctions.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about endothelial cell function.

claim: The nuclear-localized LINC complex protein SUN1 regulates vascular sprouting and endothelial cell-cell junction morphology and function.
source: Here, we show that the nuclear-localized linker of the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) complex protein SUN1 regulates vascular sprouting and endothelial cell-cell junction morphology and function.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by multiple experimental approaches shown in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of murine endothelial Sun1 impaired blood vessel formation and destabilized junctions.
source: Loss of murine endothelial Sun1 impaired blood vessel formation and destabilized junctions
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data from Sun1iECKO mice shown in Figure 1.

claim: Angiogenic sprouts formed but retracted in SUN1-depleted sprouts.
source: angiogenic sprouts formed but retracted in SUN1-depleted sprouts
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 2 and Videos 1-2.

claim: Zebrafish vessels lacking Sun1b had aberrant junctions and defective cell-cell connections.
source: zebrafish vessels lacking Sun1b had aberrant junctions and defective cell-cell connections
evidence: This is supported by zebrafish morpholino and mutant experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: SUN1 stabilized endothelial cell-cell junctions at the cellular level.
source: At the cellular level, SUN1 stabilized endothelial cell-cell junctions
evidence: This is supported by junction reformation assays and VE-cadherin localization studies shown in Figure 4.

claim: SUN1 promoted junction function.
source: promoted junction function
evidence: This is supported by impedance measurements and biotin matrix labeling assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: SUN1 regulated contractility.
source: and regulated contractility
evidence: This is supported by ppMLC staining and pharmacological inhibition experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: SUN1 depletion altered cell behaviors via the cytoskeleton without changing transcriptional profiles.
source: Mechanistically, SUN1 depletion altered cell behaviors via the cytoskeleton without changing transcriptional profiles.
evidence: This is supported by RNASeq data shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and cytoskeletal analyses in Figure 5.

claim: Reduced peripheral microtubule density accompanied SUN1 loss.
source: Reduced peripheral microtubule density, fewer junction contacts, and increased catastrophes accompanied SUN1 loss
evidence: This is supported by high-resolution imaging of microtubules shown in Figure 5C-F.

claim: Fewer junction contacts accompanied SUN1 loss.
source: Reduced peripheral microtubule density, fewer junction contacts, and increased catastrophes accompanied SUN1 loss
evidence: This is supported by quantification of microtubule-VE-cadherin contacts shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Increased catastrophes accompanied SUN1 loss.
source: Reduced peripheral microtubule density, fewer junction contacts, and increased catastrophes accompanied SUN1 loss
evidence: This is supported by EB3 tip tracking experiments shown in Figure 5G-K and Videos 5-6.

claim: Microtubule depolymerization phenocopied effects on junctions.
source: and microtubule depolymerization phenocopied effects on junctions
evidence: This is supported by nocodazole treatment experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Depletion of GEF-H1 rescued defective junctions of SUN1-depleted endothelial cells.
source: Depletion of GEF-H1, a microtubule-regulated Rho activator, or the LINC complex protein nesprin-1 rescued defective junctions of SUN1-depleted endothelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by co-depletion experiments shown in Figure 6G-J.

claim: Depletion of nesprin-1 rescued defective junctions of SUN1-depleted endothelial cells.
source: Depletion of GEF-H1, a microtubule-regulated Rho activator, or the LINC complex protein nesprin-1 rescued defective junctions of SUN1-depleted endothelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by co-depletion experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Endothelial SUN1 regulates peripheral cell-cell junctions from the nucleus via LINC complex-based microtubule interactions.
source: Thus, endothelial SUN1 regulates peripheral cell-cell junctions from the nucleus via LINC complex-based microtubule interactions that affect peripheral microtubule dynamics and Rho-regulated contractility
evidence: This is a synthesis of multiple experimental findings including microtubule dynamics, GEF-H1 localization, and nesprin-1 rescue experiments.

claim: SUN1 regulation affects peripheral microtubule dynamics and Rho-regulated contractility.
source: that affect peripheral microtubule dynamics and Rho-regulated contractility
evidence: This is supported by microtubule tracking, GEF-H1 localization, RhoA activity assays, and contractility measurements shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Long-range regulation by SUN1 is important for proper blood vessel sprouting and junction integrity.
source: and this long-range regulation is important for proper blood vessel sprouting and junction integrity
evidence: This is supported by in vivo mouse and zebrafish data showing vascular defects with SUN1 loss, shown in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: During angiogenesis, endothelial cell-cell junctions destabilize and rearrange to allow for repolarization and migration toward pro-angiogenic cues.
source: During angiogenesis, endothelial cell-cell junctions destabilize and rearrange to allow for repolarization and migration toward pro-angiogenic cues (Esser et al., 1998; Dejana, 2004; Blum et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The endothelial cell adherens junction protein VE-cadherin is required for vascular sprouting and viability.
source: Specifically, the endothelial cell adherens junction protein VE-cadherin is required for vascular sprouting and viability (Carmeliet et al., 1999; Montero-Balaguer et al., 2009; Sauteur et al., 2014; Szymborska and Gerhardt, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: As vessels mature, endothelial cell junctions stabilize and form a functional barrier that regulates egress of fluid and oxygen.
source: As vessels mature, endothelial cell junctions stabilize and form a functional barrier that regulates egress of fluid and oxygen; barrier dysfunction leads to increased permeability and severe disease (Claesson-Welsh, 2015; Rho et al., 2017; Claesson-Welsh et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Barrier dysfunction leads to increased permeability and severe disease.
source: barrier dysfunction leads to increased permeability and severe disease (Claesson-Welsh, 2015; Rho et al., 2017; Claesson-Welsh et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Regulation of endothelial cell junction stability is important developmentally and for vascular homeostasis.
source: Thus, regulation of endothelial cell junction stability is important developmentally and for vascular homeostasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited literature and established knowledge about vascular biology.

claim: Adherens junctions integrate and regulate both external and internal cellular inputs from multiple sources, including the microtubule and actin cytoskeletons.
source: Adherens junctions are key to integrating and regulating both external and internal cellular inputs from multiple sources, including the microtubule and actin cytoskeletons (Ligon et al., 2001; Shaw et al., 2007; Bellett et al., 2009; Dejana and Vestweber, 2013; Abu Taha and Schnittler, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Increased actomyosin contractility destabilizes endothelial cell adherens junctions.
source: For example, increased actomyosin contractility destabilizes endothelial cell adherens junctions, and disorganized junctional actin accompanies VE-cadherin loss (Huveneers et al., 2012; Sauteur et al., 2014; Angulo-Urarte et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Disorganized junctional actin accompanies VE-cadherin loss.
source: and disorganized junctional actin accompanies VE-cadherin loss (Huveneers et al., 2012; Sauteur et al., 2014; Angulo-Urarte et al., 2018)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: VE-cadherin loss changes microtubule dynamics.
source: VE-cadherin loss also changes microtubule dynamics, and disruption of microtubule dynamics destabilizes junctions and barrier function (Komarova et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Disruption of microtubule dynamics destabilizes junctions and barrier function.
source: and disruption of microtubule dynamics destabilizes junctions and barrier function (Komarova et al., 2012)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Coordination of inputs from the actin and microtubule cytoskeletons regulates endothelial cell barrier integrity and sprouting dynamics via small GTPases.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: RhoA signaling is regulated by microtubules via GEF-H1, a RhoGEF that is inactive while bound to microtubules and activated upon release.
source: In particular, RhoA signaling is regulated by microtubules via GEF-H1, a RhoGEF that is inactive while bound to microtubules and activated upon release, leading to RhoA activation, increased actomyosin contractility, and changes to endothelial cell barrier function (Krendel et al., 2002; Birukova et al., 2006; Birkenfeld et al., 2008).

claim: GEF-H1 activation leads to RhoA activation, increased actomyosin contractility, and changes to endothelial cell barrier function.

claim: The nucleus is important for functions critical to angiogenesis and vascular remodeling, such as polarity, migration, and mechanotransduction.

claim: Perturbations of some nuclear membrane proteins affect transcriptional profiles.

claim: The LINC complex functions as a bridge between the nucleus and the cytoskeleton.
source: that function as a bridge between the nucleus and the cytoskeleton, and also link through subnuclear lamin filaments to chromatin (Haque et al., 2006)

claim: SUN proteins provide a structural link from the nuclear cortex to the cellular cytoskeleton.

claim: Nesprins are long spectrin-rich proteins localized to the outer nuclear envelope.
source: Nesprins are long spectrin-rich proteins localized to the outer nuclear envelope that bind SUN proteins via their C-terminus while N-terminally interacting indirectly with microtubules (via various motor proteins such as dynein and kinesin) and intermediate filaments (via plectins), and directly with actin via calponin homology domains (Ketema et al., 2007; Meyerzon et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2009; Fridolfsson et al., 2010; Starr and Fridolfsson, 2010).

claim: Nesprins bind SUN proteins via their C-terminus.

claim: No significant difference between SUN1 KD and control junctions was seen at early times post-washout in the junction reformation assay.
source: No significant difference between SUN1 KD and control junctions was seen at early times post-washout, indicating that SUN1 depletion does not affect adherens junction formation (Figure 4G–H).

claim: SUN1 depletion does not affect adherens junction formation.
source: indicating that SUN1 depletion does not affect adherens junction formation
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of differences at early timepoints in the junction reformation assay.

claim: Later times post-washout revealed a significant increase in serrated junctions and gaps between endothelial cells in SUN1 KD monolayers relative to controls.
source: However, later times post-washout revealed a significant increase in serrated junctions and gaps between endothelial cells in SUN1 KD monolayers relative to controls (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: This finding is supported by the EDTA washout assay shown in Figure 4G-H.

claim: SUN1 KD endothelial cells had increased VE-cadherin internalization at steady state.
source: Consistent with these findings, SUN1 KD endothelial cells also had increased VE-cadherin internalization at steady state, consistent with actively remodeling junctions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: This finding is supported by VE-cadherin internalization assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F-G.

claim: Increased VE-cadherin internalization is consistent with actively remodeling junctions.
source: consistent with actively remodeling junctions
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about VE-cadherin internalization and junction dynamics.

claim: SUN1 is not required to form endothelial cell-cell junctions but is necessary for proper junction maturation and stabilization.
source: Thus, SUN1 is not required to form endothelial cell-cell junctions but is necessary for proper junction maturation and stabilization.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the junction formation and stabilization experiments.

claim: RNASeq analysis of HUVEC under both static and flow conditions revealed essentially no significant changes in RNA profiles except for SUN1 itself.
source: To our surprise, RNASeq analysis of HUVEC under both static and flow conditions revealed essentially no significant changes in RNA profiles except for SUN1 itself (Table 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This finding is supported by RNASeq data shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Extensive expression changes in both up and downregulated genes were documented between control HUVEC in static vs. laminar flow conditions.
source: while in the same experiment we documented extensive expression changes in both up and downregulated genes between control HUVEC in static vs. laminar flow conditions, as we and others have shown (Conway et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2021; Maurya et al., 2021; Ruter et al., 2021)
evidence: This finding is supported by RNASeq data and citations to prior literature.

claim: Re-analysis of HeLa cell data revealed few significant changes in gene expression following SUN1 depletion.
source: These findings are similar to a re-analysis of HeLa cell data (data not shown; Li et al., 2017) that revealed few significant changes in gene expression following SUN1 depletion.
evidence: This statement is based on re-analysis of published data.

claim: SUN1 is not required for nuclear communication that affects gene expression in endothelial cells.
source: Thus, although the LINC complex is important for nuclear communication that can affect gene expression, SUN1 is not required for this communication in endothelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RNASeq results showing no transcriptional changes with SUN1 depletion.

claim: Microtubule depolymerization via nocodazole treatment phenocopied SUN1 KD and destabilized adherens junctions in control monolayers.
source: Microtubule depolymerization via nocodazole treatment phenocopied SUN1 KD and destabilized adherens junctions in control monolayers but did not exacerbate the junction defects seen with SUN1 KD (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This finding is supported by nocodazole treatment experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Nocodazole treatment did not exacerbate the junction defects seen with SUN1 KD.
source: but did not exacerbate the junction defects seen with SUN1 KD (Figure 5A–B)
evidence: This finding is supported by nocodazole treatment experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Endothelial cell junction defects are downstream of microtubule perturbations induced by SUN1 depletion.
source: These findings suggest that endothelial cell junction defects are downstream of microtubule perturbations induced by SUN1 depletion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nocodazole phenocopy experiments.

claim: Significantly fewer microtubules reached the cell periphery in SUN1-depleted cells.
source: We next investigated how SUN1 affects microtubule localization in endothelial cell monolayers and found that significantly fewer microtubules reached the cell periphery or surrounded the nucleus in SUN1-depleted cells (Figure 5C and E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This finding is supported by high-resolution imaging of microtubules shown in Figure 5C, E.

claim: Significantly fewer microtubules surrounded the nucleus in SUN1-depleted cells.
source: or surrounded the nucleus in SUN1-depleted cells (Figure 5C and E, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This finding is supported by imaging shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Changes in peripheral microtubule localization were accompanied by significantly fewer microtubule-junction contacts.
source: The changes in peripheral microtubule localization were accompanied by significantly fewer microtubule-junction contacts, while α-tubulin levels around the MTOC were not affected (Figure 5C–D and F).
evidence: This finding is supported by quantification of microtubule-junction contacts shown in Figure 5F.

claim: α-tubulin levels around the MTOC were not affected by SUN1 depletion.
source: while α-tubulin levels around the MTOC were not affected (Figure 5C–D and F)
evidence: This finding is supported by quantification shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Microtubules in SUN1-depleted cells had increased shrinkage rates coupled with increased catastrophe rate and time spent shrinking.
source: Microtubules in SUN1-depleted cells had increased shrinkage rates (a more negative value) coupled with increased catastrophe rate and time spent shrinking (Figure 5G–K, Video 5 and Video 6 )
evidence: This finding is supported by EB3 tip tracking experiments shown in Figure 5G-K and Videos 5-6.

claim: Increased shrinkage rates, catastrophe rate, and time spent shrinking are consistent with elevated microtubule depolymerization and impaired microtubule dynamics downstream of SUN1 loss.
source: consistent with elevated microtubule depolymerization and impaired microtubule dynamics downstream of SUN1 loss

evidence: This is a synthesis of the microtubule analysis findings.

claim: SUN1 depletion led to ectopic stress fibers, distinct radial actin bundles at the periphery, and increased phosphorylated myosin light chain.
source: We hypothesized that actomyosin mis-regulation induced by SUN1 depletion contributes to endothelial cell junction destabilization and found that SUN1 depletion led to ectopic stress fibers, distinct radial actin bundles at the periphery, and increased phosphorylated myosin light chain (ppMLC), consistent with increased actomyosin contractility (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This finding is supported by actin and ppMLC staining shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Ectopic stress fibers, radial actin bundles, and increased ppMLC are consistent with increased actomyosin contractility.
source: consistent with increased actomyosin contractility
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about actin structures and contractility markers.

claim: Pharmacological blockade of myosin-II ATPase rescued the destabilized cell junctions, ectopic stress fibers, and radial actin structures seen with SUN1 depletion.
source: Pharmacological blockade of myosin-II ATPase rescued the destabilized cell junctions, ectopic stress fibers, and radial actin structures seen with SUN1 depletion (Figure 6A–B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This finding is supported by blebbistatin treatment experiments shown in Figure 6A-B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Rescue by myosin-II ATPase blockade suggests that SUN1 depletion increases contractility.
source: suggesting that SUN1 depletion increases contractility
evidence: This is an inference based on the blebbistatin rescue experiments.

claim: Thrombin treatment that induces contractility produced disorganized junctions in controls that phenocopied SUN1 depletion.
source: In contrast, thrombin treatment that induces contractility produced disorganized junctions in controls that phenocopied SUN1 depletion but did not contribute to further junction destabilization in SUN1 KD cells, indicating that SUN1 loss induces a maximal contractile state (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This finding is supported by thrombin treatment experiments shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: Thrombin treatment did not contribute to further junction destabilization in SUN1 KD cells.
source: but did not contribute to further junction destabilization in SUN1 KD cells
evidence: This finding is supported by thrombin treatment experiments shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: SUN1 loss induces a maximal contractile state.
source: indicating that SUN1 loss induces a maximal contractile state
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of additive effect with thrombin treatment.

claim: SUN1 loss results in hypercontractility and destabilized cell-cell junctions.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that SUN1 loss results in hypercontractility and destabilized cell-cell junctions.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the contractility experiments.

claim: SUN1 silencing increases RhoA activity in HeLa cells.
source: SUN1 silencing increases RhoA activity in HeLa cells (Thakar et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of Rho kinase (ROCK) signaling in SUN1-depleted endothelial cells rescued the destabilized cell-cell junctions and prevented the radial actin structures.
source: and pharmacological inhibition of Rho kinase (ROCK) signaling in SUN1-depleted endothelial cells rescued the destabilized cell-cell junctions and prevented the radial actin structures (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C)
evidence: This finding is supported by Y-27632 treatment experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: RhoA signaling and barrier function in endothelial cells is regulated by the microtubule-associated RhoGEF, GEF-H1.
source: RhoA signaling and barrier function in endothelial cells is regulated by the microtubule-associated RhoGEF, GEF-H1, which is inactive while bound to microtubules and peaks in activation following microtubule depolymerization and release into the cytosol (Krendel et al., 2002; Birukova et al., 2006; Birkenfeld et al., 2008; Azoitei et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: GEF-H1 is inactive while bound to microtubules and peaks in activation following microtubule depolymerization and release into the cytosol.
source: which is inactive while bound to microtubules and peaks in activation following microtubule depolymerization and release into the cytosol (Krendel et al., 2002; Birukova et al., 2006; Birkenfeld et al., 2008; Azoitei et al., 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Increased activated Rho was found with SUN1 silencing that was abrogated when GEF-H1 was also depleted.

claim: GEF-H1 signaling is upstream of elevated RhoA activation in SUN1-depleted cells.
source: suggesting that GEF-H1 signaling is upstream of elevated RhoA activation in SUN1-depleted cells
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue of RhoA activation by GEF-H1 depletion.

claim: GEF-H1 strongly localized to peripheral microtubules in control cells.

evidence: This finding is supported by GEF-H1 localization analysis shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: GEF-H1 was significantly less localized to microtubules and more diffuse in the cytosol in SUN1-depleted endothelial cells.
source: but was significantly less localized and more diffuse in the cytosol in SUN1-depleted endothelial cells (Figure 6E–F)
evidence: This finding is supported by GEF-H1 localization analysis shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Diffuse GEF-H1 localization suggests its release from microtubules.
source: suggesting its release from microtubules
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed GEF-H1 localization pattern.

source: Furthermore, depletion of GEF-H1 in endothelial cells that were also depleted for SUN1 rescued the destabilized cell-cell junctions and loss of junction integrity observed with SUN1 KD alone (Figure 6G–J)

claim: GEF-H1 acts downstream of changes in the microtubule cytoskeleton in SUN1-depleted cells.
source: indicating that GEF-H1 acts downstream of changes in the microtubule cytoskeleton in SUN1-depleted cells
evidence: This is an inference based on the inability of GEF-H1 depletion to rescue microtubule defects.

claim: SUN1 provides a novel linkage from the LINC complex to cell junctions via the microtubule cytoskeleton.
source: providing a novel linkage from the LINC complex to cell junctions via the microtubule cytoskeleton
